author: TEDx Talks
description:
For Mrs. Thushara Srinivasan, Bharatanatyam has never been just a dance form. It has been a lifelong journey of discovering purpose, overcoming limitations, and becoming the person she is today. In this talk, she reflects on how movement, when pursued with sincerity, discipline, and commitment, gradually transforms into meaning.

Drawing from deeply personal experiences, Mrs. Srinivasan shares how dance helped her overcome fear, shaped her identity as a teacher and performer, and taught her lessons that extended far beyond the stage. From finding joy beyond applause to realizing that purpose is discovered through consistent practice rather than instant answers, she illustrates how every meaningful pursuit has the power to transform us from within.

A Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi artist, educator, researcher, and storyteller, Mrs. Srinivasan reminds us that purpose is not something we search for overnight. It is cultivated through dedication, humility, and showing up every day. Her talk
title: When movement becomes meaning | Thushara Srinivasan | TEDxIIM Raipur

In a world that is more connected than ever, understanding different cultures begins with understanding the people behind them. In this talk, Archit Ojha explores how a strong sense of purpose can bridge the gap between global perspectives and local realities.

Driven by a personal mission to visit every UN-recognized country, Archit shares how his travels have gone far beyond collecting passport stamps. Through stories from across the world, he reflects on how every culture, community, and nation offers a different way of seeing life, challenging assumptions and expanding our understanding of what connects us as humans.

Drawing from his work across international development and governance, as well as his experiences engaging with diverse communities, Archit highlights how meaningful global impact is built through curiosity, empathy, and genuine human connections. His talk is a reminder that when we discover our own "Why," we become more open to understanding the "Why" of others, cre
title: Finding my why beyond borders | Archit Ojha | TEDxIIM Raipur

How can we solve society's biggest challenges without making them worse? In this TEDx talk, Sinit Zeru draws on her experience in public policy to explore why well-intentioned solutions often fail. Through compelling real-world examples, she introduces four principles for designing more effective and humane policies: question who defines the problem, embrace complexity before simplifying, recognise the limits of our own perspectives, and lead with compassion. Her talk offers a fresh framework for tackling complex social issues with greater wisdom, inclusion, and impact.
 Sinit Zeru is a Strategic Policy Advisor with 15+ years’ experience across countries and sectors. She leads specialist advisory teams at the Tony Blair Institute, focusing on government digital transformation to improve citizen services. title: Policy Principles to Heal the World | Sinit Zeru | TEDxSandford Intl School Youth

description:
¿Qué tienen en común una aldea en la República Democrática del Congo, un barrio de Sevilla y una joven ingeniera enamorada del sol? Ana Moreno lleva años convencida de que la energía solar era el "Santo Grial" para salvar el mundo. Hasta que la realidad le dio una lección: 460 paneles en perfecto estado, declarados residuos, atrapados por el sistema justo cuando más falta hacían. Pero entonces algo inesperado ocurrió. 

Y cuando Ana descubrió quién estaba detrás, entendió por fin de qué energía estaba hablando todo el tiempo.
 Vivimos en una era obsesionada con encontrar la fuente que garantice nuestra supervivencia y sostenibilidad. El debate global se centra en cables, paneles y átomos, pero Ana Moreno, Embajadora del Pacto Climático Europeo y Consultora en Desarrollo Sostenible, nos propone un giro radical para redescubrir el recurso más potente y desaprovechado de la sociedad. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a loca
title: La energía del futuro será humana, el motor que nace en Sevilla | Ana Moreno | TEDxCIS SFP Youth

description:
I'm thirteen. And I look at school and wonder: what world is it preparing us for? Marco has spent two years watching artificial intelligence go from a curious toy to a tool capable of writing essays, solving problems, and improving its own code. If answers are everywhere, what's the point of school still testing our ability to memorise them? In this talk, Marco isn't here to complain about technology. He's here to propose something harder: changing what we understand by learning. Less "repeat and don't make mistakes." More "think, verify, build." Because his generation doesn't just need to adapt to the future. It needs to shape it.
 Marco is a 13-year-old Italian and Spanish student with excellent academic performance, maintaining an average of 9.5 out of 10. He speaks Italian, Spanish, and English fluently, and is also studying Chinese. He has been playing volleyball for four years, an experience that has taught him discipline, teamwork, and perseverance. He is also passionate about
title: The last homework  | Marco Petricciuolo | TEDxCIS SFP Youth

Did you know that almost 28% of the world's population is afraid of flying? One of the most common fears is that of a mid-air collision. But there's a system working in silence, aboard every commercial flight, to make sure that never happens. In this talk, Alejandro takes us from the congested skies of the 1950s to the technology that redefined aviation safety: TCAS (Traffic Collision Avoidance System). It started as a small project with low expectations, in the hands of a handful of engineers, and went on to become one of the most consequential advances in modern aviation A story about how quiet ideas can change the world.

description:
In this inspiring TEDx presentation, the speaker explores the powerful impact of using privilege for the service of others through the legacy of Countess Viktoria von Butler-Haimhausen. Born into extraordinary wealth and influence in 19th-century Bavaria, Viktoria transformed her personal experiences with profound family loss into a life dedicated to social reform and advocacy. From establishing schools and shelters for marginalized women and the elderly to fighting for gender equality on an international stage, her story challenges us to look beyond our own comfort. The presentation leaves the audience with a compelling question: how will we choose to use our own unique influence, knowledge, and resources to build a better life for those around us?

Backed by compelling data on the value of diverse perspectives, she delivers a moving call to action for viewers to shift their mindsets—urging us to look beyond superficial standards, celebrate the beauty of human differences, and measure true beauty by the positive impact we leave on the world. description: In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Tara Delić explores the fundamental question of what it means to be human by contrasting our core instinct to care with the protective behaviors we develop out of fear. Drawing from the history of Homo sapiens and Neanderthals, as well as personal anecdotes and recent student-led movements in Serbia, Delić introduces the concept of the "lenses" through which we view the world—shaped by experiences of empathy, kindness, and pain. She argues that society often forces us to build protective layers around our authentic, creative, and compassionate cores, leading to detachment and systemic oppression. Ultimately, Delić delivers an inspiring call to action, reminding us that genuine societal change is a marathon built on the collective efforts of dreamers, and encourages us to reconnect with our humanity by choosing empathy over fear. What happens when we redefine beauty not as a standard of vanity, but as an engine for economic liberation? This compelling talk challenges the traditional boundaries of entrepreneurship, shifting the narrative from corporate banking to a grassroots movement called "Womenocracy." By identifying a deep-seated cultural gap for South Asian women, the idea explores how spaces traditionally meant for aesthetics can be re-engineered into sanctuaries of education, financial independence, and mental wellness. It proves that true empowerment isn't just about looking good—it is about creating an economic pipeline that lifts hundreds of young girls out of dependency. 

This talk serves as a blueprint for modern ambition, offering a provocative look at how we can shatter glass ceilings, maximize our grandest life goals, and scale social impact simply by choosing to build ladders for others as we climb. The talk outlines the five distinct phases of human life, creating a roadmap for a unique and purposeful journey. Life begins with an initial observation phase that transitions into exploration, where the very first lesson taught is to love, which then guides an individual to explore their future career path. This evolves into the learning phase, a timeless process requiring people to break out of their comfort zones, which leads directly into the experience phase where true wisdom is gained by doing. It is within this experiential stage that one must align the "3 Ps of Life" Personality, Profession, and Passion—to unlock an extraordinary existence, emphasizing the philosophy to "be only one, not number one" by cultivating absolute uniqueness rather than competing with others. 

The journey concludes with the fourth phase of effectively marketing oneself to the world, and finally, a phase of deep contemplation to reflect on one's impact, proving that true success comes from living wit
title: Be Only One, Not Number One: The 5 Phases of a Purposeful Life | Haseeb Khan | TEDxGIU

Amani Jannat shares her remarkable ascent from an eight-year-old enthusiast to a national champion and the historic first Pakistani female to compete internationally at the Asian Games. Emphasizing that sports climbing is now an internationally recognized Olympic discipline, Amani attributes her meteoric rise not to a desire for trophies, but to a deeply rooted hunger for continuous learning and self-mastery.
